rules.title: Repeated authentication failures
rules.description: At least 5 failed authentications for the same user from the same source in 5 minutes.
rules.threshold: 5 failures / 5 minutes / same user + source IP
recommended_actions: Verify whether the source and target user are expected.
Check adjacent authentication events and endpoint telemetry.
If unauthorized, block or rate-limit the source through approved controls and reset affected credentials.
investigation_questions: Is the source IP a known internal subnet, corporate VPN, or external IP?
Has the target user reported forgetting their password or having sync issues?
Are there simultaneous failures across other protocols (e.g., Kerberos, NTLM, OAuth)?

rules.title: Password spraying pattern
rules.description: At least 8 distinct user accounts fail authentication from one source within 10 minutes.
rules.threshold: 8 distinct users / 10 minutes / same source IP
recommended_actions: Check whether the source is a known corporate proxy, VPN, or identity provider.
Review targeted accounts for subsequent successful logins.
Apply approved rate limiting and MFA protections; avoid blocking shared infrastructure without validation.
investigation_questions: Is the source IP a legitimate outbound proxy, SaaS gateway, or identity provider proxy?
Are usernames being targeted alphabetically or sequentially (sign of dictionary enumeration)?
Did any targeted account successfully log in during or immediately after the spray window?

rules.title: Successful login after repeated failures
rules.description: A successful authentication follows at least 5 failures for the same user from the same source within 10 minutes.
rules.threshold: success within 10 minutes after 5+ failures / same user + source IP
recommended_actions: Validate the successful login with the account owner and expected source/location.
Review MFA result, device posture, session activity, and the next 15 minutes of events.
If compromise is suspected, revoke sessions and rotate credentials using the incident-response process.
investigation_questions: Did the user satisfy MFA requirements on the successful login?
Does the device fingerprint / user-agent match the user's historical profile?
What actions were performed in the first 15 minutes following the successful authentication?

rules.title: Privilege change after suspicious authentication
rules.description: A privileged role change occurs within 15 minutes of a suspicious login sequence for the same user.
rules.threshold: privilege change within 15 minutes after suspicious authentication
recommended_actions: Confirm the role change against an approved change ticket and authorized administrator.
Inspect identity-provider audit logs and actions taken with the new privilege.
If unauthorized, remove the grant, revoke sessions, preserve evidence, and escalate to the incident lead.
investigation_questions: Is there an approved change management ticket corresponding to this privilege grant?
Was the grant performed by an authorized system administrator or from an administrative console?
Has the newly assigned role been used to access sensitive assets or modify other accounts?

rules.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) denial anomaly
rules.description: At least 2 MFA prompts were denied/rejected for the same user within 10 minutes (MFA fatigue or prompt spamming indicator).
recommended_actions: Contact the user out-of-band to confirm if they rejected MFA prompts.
Review identity provider logs for MFA challenge types and push delivery status.
Reset user credentials and temporarily require number matching or FIDO2 tokens if prompt bombing is active.
investigation_questions: Did the user report receiving unsolicited MFA pushes or phone calls?
Did an MFA approval eventually occur after multiple denials?
What IP sources originated the authentication attempts triggering MFA?

rules.title: Distributed credential attack on single account
rules.description: At least 4 distinct source IPs fail authentication against the same target user within 15 minutes.
rules.threshold: 4 distinct source IPs / 15 minutes / same user
recommended_actions: Assess if the account is subject to a targeted credential stuffing or botnet campaign.
Check whether password protection / smart lockout has engaged for the account.
Enforce conditional access policies and review geo-velocity anomalies.
investigation_questions: Are the source IPs part of a known botnet, VPN proxy pool, or TOR exit nodes?
Is the target user a high-profile executive, administrator, or VIP account?
Are there successful logins for this account from any of the distributed sources?
